title: Plans vs Predictions
objectives: Use plans vs predictions accurately in A2 contexts.
Understand form, meaning, and typical usage.
Produce short spoken and written examples.
canDo: I can choose between will, going to, and present continuous.

warmUp.title: Activate prior knowledge
warmUp.prompt: Before this lesson, recall what you know about plans vs predictions. How is it similar or different from Portuguese?
reflectionQuestions: When do native speakers use plans vs predictions?
Can you think of one example?

explanation: Plan/intention → going to | Arrangement with time → present continuous | Prediction/spontaneous → will

grammar.title: Plans vs Predictions
grammar.rule: Plan/intention → going to | Arrangement with time → present continuous | Prediction/spontaneous → will

reading.title: Plans vs Predictions in Context
reading.text: A: What are you doing this weekend? B: I am visiting my sister — we booked tickets. A: I think it will be cold. B: In that case, I'll take a jacket. I'm going to buy one anyway.

writing.prompt: Write a short paragraph (5–7 sentences) using plans vs predictions. Use at least 3 words from the vocabulary list.
rubricHints: Use the target structure at least twice.
writing.modelAnswer: It was a quick decision. There is evidence of rain. A spontaneous offer. A fixed appointment.

tutorHints: Correct gently and ask the learner to reformulate.
Use English for meta-language when possible at A2.
